title: A generator of your own
description:
Write a small xorshift64 random number generator:

```c
typedef struct { uint64_t s; } Rng;        /* s must not be 0 */

uint64_t rng_next(Rng *r);                 /* x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >> 7; x ^= x << 17; store and return x */
uint64_t rng_below(Rng *r, uint64_t n);    /* a fair number from 0 to n - 1 (n >= 1), by rejection */
double rng_double(Rng *r);                 /* 0 <= result < 1, from the top 53 bits */
```

`rng_below` throws away values at or above `UINT64_MAX - UINT64_MAX % n` before taking `% n`, so every result is equally likely. The tests check the exact numbers, so follow the formulas.
hints: Each line of the formula is one statement on a `uint64_t`; store the result back into `r->s` and return it (lesson 8.06).
`(double)(x >> 11) / 2^53` keeps 53 random bits, exactly what a `double` can hold, so the result is always below 1.
